title: Sample: Investigate a Kubernetes pod failure
summary: Inspect pod scheduling, container state, and health before recovery.
symptoms: A pod remains pending, repeatedly restarts, or fails readiness checks.
A workload has fewer ready replicas than its declared target.

root_cause.details: Use pod events, container logs, and workload status to distinguish image, resource, scheduling, configuration, and application failures.

prerequisites: Approved read access to the relevant namespace and workload.
Confirm the cluster context and namespace before inspecting resources.
investigation_steps: Confirm the current cluster context, namespace, and affected workload.
Inspect pod status, restart counts, recent events, and container logs.
Check image availability, resource requests, scheduling constraints, and referenced configuration.
resolution_steps: Address the confirmed image, resource, configuration, or application issue through the standard deployment process.
Allow the controller to reconcile the workload and observe the replacement pod.
verification_steps: Confirm the replacement pod is ready and restart counts are stable.
Verify the workload has its expected ready replicas and passes its health checks.
rollback_steps: Roll back to the last known-good workload revision if the remediation causes additional failures.
Verify service readiness after rollback and notify the workload owner.
prevention: Use readiness and liveness probes appropriate to the workload.
Set resource requests and limits based on observed needs and alert on repeated restarts.
